class: the same finding comes back unfixed, and the reviewer must say so
origin: founding-agents-site #4 and #6 (PRs #7 and #9): the same findings came back round after round; the two stalls were 43% of the website's spend
summary: Round 2 of a review: one earlier finding is fixed, one is not. The right review marks only the unfixed one as a repeat, so build stops for the founder.

commits.message: Fail on a date that does not parse

issues.title: Site 3 of 3: the record of this build
issues.body:
Add this build's entries to the record, newest first. Tests for the record, and that it is in date order.

Holds for every site issue: every claim on the page is true on the day this merges, using the facts in `docs/status.md`; it reads at 390 px and at 1440 px.

## Technical decisions
None: copy and tests inside the existing page.

prs.title: Test the record
prs.body:
Adds tests that every record entry has a date and that the record is newest first.

Closes #6

comments.author: todd450
comments.body:
**Code review: Changes needed**

- `tests/test_record.py` `_li_count`: counts the literal text `<li>`, so an entry written `<li class="late">` is invisible to `test_every_entry_has_a_date`, and an undated entry passes. Match the element, not the text.
- `tests/test_record.py` `test_record_is_newest_first`: skips any date it cannot parse, so an entry with a malformed date passes. Fail on it instead.
